newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soybean regions remain warm and humid.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean regions remain warm and humid.

text.p: Steady showers throughout Brazil's key soybean growing regions have kept conditions optimal for the current crop, although growers in some areas said soil moisture was too high and they would welcome sunshine.
In Parana state, widespread rainfall during the weekend had created optimal conditions for the soybean crop, said Nelson Costa of cooperatives organization Ocepar.
"We have high humidity and high temperatures," he said. "The prospect is for fresh rains this week, which for the crop is excellent. Conditions are optimal."
But a technician at the Coopavel cooperative in Cascavel warned that soil moisture was already excessive and productivity could drop if rains continued apace.
Temperatures there ranged between 17 and 32 degrees Celsius and late afternoon showers were seen during the next three days.
"We need some sunshine," the technician said, adding that currently cloudy skies should clear by January 3 and bring some brighter, drier weather.
In Rio Grande do Sul, temperatures were around the 30 degree C mark with a prospect of further rainfall later in the day.
"Rainfall is not abundant but it is sufficient," said Sergio Gregory of the Santa Barbara cooperative. "The soybeans are growing relatively fast, the plants are very robust."
